title: The Jackal and the Otters
text:
Two otters were hunting along a river. One of them, swimming in deep water, seized a huge fish, so big and strong that it began to drag him under. He called to his partner, and together they wrestled the fish to the bank and killed it.

Then the trouble began. Each otter said the fish was his. One had caught it, the other had saved it. They quarrelled loudly and could not agree how to divide it.

Just then a jackal came down to the river to drink. The otters asked him to settle their dispute. The jackal sat down with a judicious air and gave his verdict. To the otter who had swum along the bank he gave the tail. To the one who had gone into the deep water he gave the head. "And the middle," he said, "goes to the judge for his fee." He picked up the whole fat body of the fish and trotted off with it.

The two otters sat looking at a head and a tail. They admitted that had they not quarrelled, the whole fish would have fed them both for days.
lesson: When partners fight over shares, an outsider often ends up with the best part. Settle disagreements between yourselves before you need someone else to do it.
